mechanisms.title: Event taxonomy and vocabulary ownership
mechanisms.problem: Event-driven hosts conflate events that have different jobs (durable replayable facts, live runtime signals, notifications) and let multiple verbs or mirrored event types encode one policy. Adding a producer then forces edits to central switches, and a consumer cannot tell which events are durable, which are transient, and which package owns their payload rules.
triggers: A new event family, producer plugin, or dispatch mode is proposed
Two verbs or events appear to perform nearly the same user action
A consumer needs to distinguish durable facts from live-only signals
obligations: Separate event domains by job: durable session facts are JSON-only and replayable; live agent/runtime events carry runtime identity and interception; notifications are fire-and-forget
Keep the event vocabulary in contract packages and use a small pure Cordis taxonomy: waterfall, serial, parallel, and emit, each with one owner
Allow exactly one concrete loop plugin; nothing else re-dispatches the loop's events
Make the durable event map merge-extensible so a producer package owns its event type, payload declaration merge, and an invariant companion
Collapse near-parallel verbs into one primitive plus preset aliases; coalesce duplicate message event types
Place a goal mutation on the durable side when it must survive restart and fork regardless of model admission, and keep inbox delivery separate

Treat wakeup as the sole should-the-model-run signal: a lone `next-turn` or no-wakeup item stays parked and rides the next waking send, every insertion and exit publishes its matching live notification, and domain-specific durable facts travel in typed message sources rather than a parallel metadata channel.
steps: Classify the event by job and lifetime
Choose the narrowest dispatch mode and name its policy
Put the type, payload merge, and invariant rules in the producing package
Register through the declared extension point, not a central union edit
Delete parallel verbs and mirrored event types, migrating consumers to the primitive

enforcement.mode: Type-checked declaration merging plus producer invariant tests
enforcement.implementation: The sole concrete loop plugin is enforced by composition and review; package boundaries and dependency gates constrain who may emit
enforcement.trust: Payload restrictions are trusted to the producer's invariant companion; the loop does not guess business rules
enforcement.failure: Missing merge or a second loop plugin fails typecheck/composition; a consumer that cannot classify an event must reject it rather than default it
enforcement.exceptions: Product-specific event names and payloads may differ; the taxonomy is transferable, the vocabulary is not

mechanisms.applicability: Hosts with durable replay plus live runtime signals and multiple event-producing plugins.

migration.strategy: Reclassify event families before adding producers; keep compatibility only while a named consumer exists
migration.implementation: Introduce the merge-extensible map and one dispatch taxonomy, move payload invariants to producers, then remove parallel verbs
migration.requiredSupport: A typed declaration-merge mechanism, a single loop composition point, and consumer tests for domain classification

positive.scenario: Adding a producer requires no central switch edit and each event has one owning package

rejection.scenario: A consumer that receives a durable event without its invariant companion, or a live event claiming durability, is rejected

recovery.scenario: A producer removed from the registry removes its declarations without leaving mirrored vocabulary; consumers fall back only through an explicit unknown path

mechanisms.title: Event-log integrity and format governance
mechanisms.problem: Storing conversation facts as ad hoc records or parallel persisted message types allows crashes to truncate turns, publish half-written files, let readers disagree about field meaning, and let projection checkpoints grow with message count. Contradictory metadata can make the model history and diagnostics report different outcomes.
triggers: A new durable event, format version, or persistence provider is added
A crash, fork, import, or migration must not lose or silently reshape facts
A projection or cached read model is derived from the log
obligations: Keep an append-only log of typed events as the sole source of truth; derive message history from it
Represent persistence as a capability seam over the existing event type, never a parallel persisted-message type
Close a crashed turn instead of truncating the log; the reader owns balancing and synthesis

Publish durable files atomically per platform: POSIX temp file, fsync, link, directory fsync, unlink temp; Windows staging directory plus MoveFileExW write-through without replace/copy flags, with a fork-publication protocol before namespace mutation
Use one monotonic format version with the first shipped reader as the permanent floor; convert only at the released edge

Require one canonical envelope at every ingress: required surface placement, exactly append or a replace span in current surface order, membership/order/coverage checks, and no alternate spellings in current readers
Reject contradictory records rather than repairing them, and validate cross-event relationships such as a result's advertised call or a checkpoint's compaction
Retain only non-derivable projection state (surviving system prompts, one running total, at most one armed shadow-price claim); version the state and discard old rows
Use bounded coalescing measured from the first pending event, not a resetting debounce, and keep the window as internal scheduling policy
Order sidecar writes with a durability barrier and per-item compare-and-swap; keep feedback out of the canonical log
Treat derivation cost as structural: compaction, not log mutation, mitigates growth, and the durable event shape stays frozen once released.

Preserve immutable unknown attribution through validation; breaking representation changes need a successor, compatible additions need new acknowledgements, and fixes must preserve the declared meaning.

Retain unknown ignorable records with their payloads and original positions while validating known records even when marked ignorable; compare JSON arguments by own properties so inherited prototype members cannot satisfy recorded fields.

Keep storage metadata (format version, cwd, lineage) in an out-of-log `SessionHeader` exposed as readonly `session.header`, never in `SessionEventMap` or `deriveMessages()`; `createdAt` is a non-negative safe-integer Unix epoch milliseconds value.
steps: Define the event and envelope contract
Validate before accepting, at seed, append, restore, and browser publication
Publish atomically and prove recovery
Version the format and convert only at the boundary
Derive caches and projections with explicit state versions
Test replay equivalence and malformed-record rejection

enforcement.mode: Schema and acceptance validators at every ingress; platform-specific atomic publish; migration and replay tests
enforcement.implementation: Host owns surface membership and source existence; browser validates the envelope and delegates event-local rules to shared validators
enforcement.trust: Malformed records fail before projection rather than disappearing; publication is atomic or absent
enforcement.failure: Contradictory records are rejected, not inferred; migration gives up best-effort repair of contradictions
enforcement.exceptions: Platform filesystem behavior, Node internals, and exact format numbers are version-specific; event-local versus relationship validation ownership must stay explicit

mechanisms.applicability: Any durable event-sourced system that crosses memory, disk, migration, and client readers.

migration.strategy: Separate event-local validation from log-dependent relationship validation, then put acceptance at every reader
migration.implementation: Adopt a canonical envelope plus a monotonic format version and platform atomic-publish adapter; add projection state versioning separately
migration.requiredSupport: A durable log, an atomic-publish primitive, a migration edge, and replay fixtures

positive.scenario: Equal logical evidence yields identical replay, migration, and projection results

rejection.scenario: Malformed or contradictory records are rejected before any projection or model-visible read

recovery.scenario: A failed publication leaves the previous generation intact; a crash leaves a closable turn rather than a truncated log

mechanisms.title: Capability seam ownership and evidence-gated abstraction
mechanisms.problem: Capabilities tend to accrete: a concrete registry mixes transport, policy, and business semantics; parallel context keys split one query; a seam grows several vocabularies and listener paths; or an interface is introduced before a second implementation exists, creating configuration with no consumer.
triggers: Two providers or consumers genuinely need the same capability
A concrete registry is imported across packages
A policy is enforced by asking model-facing tools to cooperate
A second real consumer appears, or a seam has accreted duplicate output/listener paths
obligations: Split Service Definition, Service Provider, and Consumer when the seam is genuinely multi-provider; the interface package owns the context key, provider registration/selection, shared request/result vocabulary, and errors
Providers register capabilities, never model-facing tools; the tool package owns the model-facing schema and dispatch
Use one abstract service on one context key; make only backend-specific methods abstract; do not add a provider registry or coordinator with no consumer
Abstraction is evidence-gated: keep one concrete implementation until a second real consumer justifies extraction; keep it a pure library when the shared concern is mechanical
Consolidate an accreted seam to one ring, one projection, and one event stream; remove duplicate vocabularies and listeners

Keep filesystem freshness policy as an optional event-gate plugin rather than a mandatory method service: shipped guarded deployments mount it, the bare provider remains usable and unconstrained, and first-wins ownership is a deployment convention with an explicit earlier-listener bypass risk

Justify a shared library by multiple real consumers; when a runtime relationship invariant would be vacuous (for example a private-file read), say so in an empty invariant companion instead of inventing a check.
When a note supersedes only one ownership decision, keep the earlier note authoritative for the remaining semantics and cite the boundary.

Announce registration before starting a producer; a synchronous first drain must not race ahead of the registration event, and a settled output ring retains every byte the model cursor has not consumed until the first terminal read.
Keep one claim per wait with a live flag cleared synchronously on abort, so a settlement announced before rejection still reaches the tool and a timed-out wait drops only its own claim.

Carry a settled outcome result exactly once on the first read after settlement, and adapt special producers (consuming readers, observed offset readers) to the same byte ring instead of adding a second representation.

Let the Service Provider derive admission capacity (`running` plus `stopping`) from the same records per exact owner, including one unowned bucket, without adding a public count or a second state owner.
Map each provider response into the seam's optional-field vocabulary and omit fields the provider did not supply instead of fabricating them or leaking vendor-specific shapes.
steps: Inventory actual providers and consumers, not hypothetical ones
Decide interface versus library versus concrete service
Move shared vocabulary and ownership to the narrow interface
Register providers explicitly at composition and forbid core name branches
Delete compatibility paths once the named consumers are migrated

enforcement.mode: Dependency gates and package boundaries; contract tests shared by providers
enforcement.implementation: The interface owner controls vocabulary; composition controls which provider is selected; core code cannot scan packages or branch on provider names
enforcement.trust: A provider that fails contract tests or a consumer importing a concrete provider is rejected by the gate
enforcement.failure: Missing provider fails composition explicitly; a policy gate refusal fails the effect before it happens
enforcement.exceptions: Cordis-specific seams and job registries are implementation context; the ownership rule transfers, exact package names do not

mechanisms.applicability: Multi-provider capabilities, plugin systems, and policy-bearing tool execution.

migration.strategy: Start from the real consumer list and one ownership sentence per seam
migration.implementation: Define the narrow interface and shared vocabulary; move policy into the in-path gate; register providers only at composition
migration.requiredSupport: A consumer inventory, a shared contract test suite, a composition registry, and a dependency gate

positive.scenario: A new provider can be added without editing consumers or core switches

rejection.scenario: A second context key, a core provider-name branch, or a bypassed policy gate is rejected by review or dependency checks

recovery.scenario: Removing a provider leaves an explicit composition error, not a silent fallback; compatibility entries have named consumers and removal conditions

mechanisms.title: Package layering and dependency direction
mechanisms.problem: Package graphs drift: a client imports host runtime, a web server depends on a workspace package, build metadata is treated as bundler instructions, a process-wide singleton serves scoped state, or a capability is placed at a plane whose lifetime and reach do not match. The resulting cycles and build-face leaks are hard to see from imports alone.
triggers: A new package, build face, or cross-plane capability is added
A client or lower layer imports a higher-layer runtime
Build output differs between source and packaged modes
obligations: Make dependency direction auditable from package manifests: client never imports host runtime; runtime to API proxy is one-way; a surface server depends on no workspace package
Keep one flat configuration tree with one row per plugin and per-surface overlays; no in-code tunables
Layer a host singleton per scope when deployment supply and agent consumption are different questions
Place a capability where its reach matches its lifecycle; move process-wide projections to a host-plane owner when the agent plane no longer fits
Let build faces, not npm dependency sections alone, define bundle externality and shared identity
Delegate TypeScript transformation to the toolchain and replace runtime checks with static gates where possible
Place each check where it can actually prove the claimed property
Make production entry points join Agents explicitly: installing a registry does not bind them, and an unjoined Agent otherwise receives no tools, prompt sections or skills without an error.
Fail before composition when a boot registration is missing, and surface later import, apply and service-wait failures through the boot status; keep runtime modules self-contained.

Treat built artifacts as the served truth: typechecking source does not prove the browser runs the same code, so add a build/watch drift check, and declare static UI libraries as explicit exceptions with their conversion prerequisites.
Let the shipped profile own the complete client package roster; individual client packages must not re-solve the same graph through peer placement.

Complete the immediately-tier prefetch before creating entries: `tree.import` materialization is a synchronous require that fiber inject waiting does not protect, so cross-package require edges need every factory registered first or boot races.
steps: Draw the intended dependency direction and write it down
Encode it in package manifests, exports, and dependency gates
Split build faces and configuration planes
Move misplaced capabilities and delete the old path
Run typecheck, module-graph, build, and packaged-artifact gates

enforcement.mode: Module-graph and dependency gates; package exports; build and packaged-artifact checks
enforcement.implementation: Layering is trusted only when mechanically checked; a review comment is not a substitute for a graph gate
enforcement.trust: A violation fails the gate before merge or packaging
enforcement.failure: A moved capability leaves an explicit composition error; no silent cross-plane fallback
enforcement.exceptions: Exact package names, bundler behavior, and toolchain versions are source-specific

mechanisms.applicability: Monorepos and plugin hosts with multiple runtime/UI/build planes.

migration.strategy: State the dependency direction and build faces first
migration.implementation: Encode gates, then split planes and move capabilities
migration.requiredSupport: A dependency graph checker, package export maps, and per-surface build configuration

positive.scenario: The manifest graph matches the documented direction and packaged artifacts contain no unintended inlining

rejection.scenario: A cross-layer import or unlisted build face fails the gate

recovery.scenario: A moved package leaves a composition failure rather than a stale duplicate

mechanisms.title: Single-source contracts and stable public faces
mechanisms.problem: Types and declarations get copied between runtime code, package manifests, client bundles, and tests. Copies drift, readers disagree about defaults, and a public plugin face renamed after external plugins exist breaks every consumer.
triggers: A contract is consumed by runtime, build metadata, and client code
A public plugin or extension face is about to be published
A manifest or declaration is parsed in more than one place
obligations: Put manifest declarations in one type-only utility package with no runtime values; readers keep parsing, validation, defaults, and resolved data
Leave runtime service and event declarations with their owning packages
Settle public faces (field names, enums, address grammar) before external plugins exist; dynamic client plugins may import only types
Use declaration merging to extend contracts instead of editing a closed union or central switch
Keep authoring interfaces and generated documentation derived from the same declaration

Separate resource addresses from navigation addresses: only the `dsh-resource://` family is a public contract, while navigation literals are package-internal bookkeeping composed in one place and never imported by business packages.
steps: Identify the single source for each contract
Move type-only declarations and remove copies
Derive validators, docs, and client types from that source
Freeze public names and add compatibility tests before publication
Delete duplicated declarations and casts

enforcement.mode: Typecheck and API snapshot tests; package type tests; generated documentation checks
enforcement.implementation: The contract package owns the declaration; runtime owners own behavior; consumers may rely only on the published face
enforcement.trust: A duplicated declaration or an unlisted public face fails type or snapshot checks
enforcement.failure: A missing declaration fails compilation; compatibility entries need a named consumer and removal condition
enforcement.exceptions: The source repository uses TypeScript declaration merging; other languages need an equivalent single-source mechanism

mechanisms.applicability: Published extension APIs and manifest-driven plugin systems.

migration.strategy: Choose the declaration owner and freeze the public face
migration.implementation: Move declarations to one type-only source, derive readers and docs, and add snapshot coverage
migration.requiredSupport: A type-only package, API snapshot tooling, and consumer compilation tests

positive.scenario: Runtime, build metadata, and client code accept the same declaration and defaults

rejection.scenario: A copy or renamed public field fails type/snapshot checks

recovery.scenario: A removed public face leaves a documented migration path rather than a silent runtime failure

mechanisms.title: Channel-independent protocol ownership
mechanisms.problem: Transport state and protocol semantics get duplicated per channel or realm. A debugger transport on a paused thread cannot deliver resume, producers each emit their own protocol state, a host protocol shares stdout with arbitrary program bytes, and downlink-only RPC forces each interactive feature to invent a second carriage and correlation key.
triggers: A protocol must work over WebSocket, in-process, worker, and native carriers
A second realm or process must observe or control the same state
An interactive operation needs client-to-host data while the operation remains active
obligations: Give protocol state one owner; adapters translate channels but do not re-implement semantics
Provide one duplex stream kind with one generation: downlink item/end/error, uplink item/end, one stream id; reopening and cursors belong to upper layers
Declare uplink and downlink item types in one compiler-visible place (the method return type) and generate strict codecs
Carry the caller identity (Peer) and cancellation in the invocation context; every carrier names its Peer explicitly
Validate frame shapes exactly, bound the uplink inbox, and fail the whole stream on overflow rather than silently dropping data
Use a dedicated control descriptor for host protocols, never stdout/stderr framing; preserve it across platforms and grant no host capability
Use read-local cancellation promises so retained state does not grow with delivered items
Close admission before disposal: stop capture, close sockets and owned upstream sessions, and wait for the owned worker to exit before reporting the endpoint disposed.
Name and test every synthetic compatibility no-op; never answer an unknown protocol method with a blanket success that hides protocol drift.
Treat loopback binding as mandatory reachability control, not authentication; bound captured bytes and state that full capture exposes credentials and payloads to any local process able to attach.

Keep one fixed control descriptor across platforms; native wrappers preserve and close it, and consumers bound control-message input and output because the subprocess service neither interprets nor buffers them.
Use a dedicated transport for integrity and ownership, not as a JavaScript security boundary; the OS sandbox and managed process owner still own confinement and teardown.
steps: Write the channel-independent protocol contract and state machine
Implement adapters for each carrier and one shared router
Add strict frame validation, bounded queues, and cancellation tests
Test the same method through multiple carriers and unchanged legacy methods

enforcement.mode: Exact-key frame validation, schema/codec checks, bounded inbox, and carrier equivalence tests
enforcement.implementation: The protocol owner defines semantics; transport adapters only encode/decode; the Host validates every uplink item
enforcement.trust: A malformed frame or overflow fails the stream/socket; an unknown stream id is ignored so in-flight frames cannot harm other streams
enforcement.failure: A carrier loss fails the stream with a carrier error and the upper layer decides whether to reopen
enforcement.exceptions: WebSocket has no per-stream write window; worker tunnels may intentionally differ (trusted same-origin, no inbox limit); no cross-direction ordering guarantee

mechanisms.applicability: RPC and streaming protocols with several carriers and interactive bidirectional operations.

migration.strategy: Separate protocol state from transport state, then add the uplink channel and invocation context
migration.implementation: Define one wire contract and state machine, implement adapters, and keep upper-layer recovery out of the transport
migration.requiredSupport: Strict codecs, a bounded queue, Peer plumbing, and multi-carrier tests

positive.scenario: The same business method behaves identically through WebSocket and in-process carriers; legacy downlink-only methods are unchanged

rejection.scenario: Malformed frames, post-end items, overflow, and decode failures fail explicitly with stable codes

recovery.scenario: A carrier loss ends the generation cleanly; reopening is an upper-layer decision with its own anchors

mechanisms.title: Configuration authority, provenance, and atomicity
mechanisms.problem: Configuration reads are often treated as harmless while writes are guarded, yet reads can expose secrets or enable DNS rebinding. A dependency's generated catalog can silently replace a declared route, partial updates can erase unrelated keys, adapter defaults can be indistinguishable from user choices, and deferrals disappear from the record.
triggers: A configuration plane, provider route, or settings namespace is added
A default is materialized into effective configuration
A UI edits part of a configuration document
A boundary decision is intentionally deferred
obligations: Treat reading configuration as privileged as writing it; trustedHosts is a DNS-rebinding fence, not an authorization boundary
Keep one flat config tree with one row per plugin and per-surface overlays; no in-code tunables
A provider route is a declaration; the installed catalog is only its default, not the configuration boundary
Mark an adapter-owned default as such when the caller omitted a value; make the marked effective config a durable request-header fact before execution
Write partial configuration losslessly and atomically; preserve unknown keys and snapshot consistency
Keep an explicit deferral ledger naming owner, trigger, and reopening condition
Interrogate a draft provider endpoint one-shot by its settings namespace when no route/profile/credential exists yet; do not enumerate unrelated namespaces
Keep the model-discovery registry minimal: one offer per namespace, no storage, and no lifecycle beyond the owning fiber; provider/network failures and malformed-URL rejection are distinct results.

A declared route may use only protocols fully describable by a key, endpoint, and headers; providers requiring SigV4, ADC, Azure environment, or OAuth authentication stay catalog-only, and authentication follows the provider rather than the wire protocol.

A settings namespace is not web-configurable until it also registers a configurable provider; its descriptor carries a required `revision`, `expectedRevision` expresses write conflicts, and clients that ignore it keep last-write-wins.
steps: Classify configuration by plane, owner, and secrecy
Define defaults and provenance markers
Validate the complete effective snapshot before use
Write atomically and losslessly; record deferrals
Expose only the sanitized fields a surface needs

enforcement.mode: Schema validation, authorization boundary tests, snapshot tests, and secret redaction
enforcement.implementation: Read access follows the same privilege as write; the Host validates before dispatch; clients never receive raw secrets
enforcement.trust: A missing/invalid required value fails closed; a read beyond the surface's authorization is rejected
enforcement.failure: A failed write leaves the previous snapshot; a deferral remains listed until its trigger closes
enforcement.exceptions: Product-specific config layouts and env names are not universal; docs outside this partition were not inspected

mechanisms.applicability: Layered configuration with secrets, provider catalogs, UI editors, and deferred decisions.

migration.strategy: Map planes, owners, defaults, and secrecy before adding fields
migration.implementation: Add provenance markers, validation, atomic writes, and a deferral ledger; update docs and tests together
migration.requiredSupport: A config schema/validator, an authorization boundary, and snapshot/write tests

positive.scenario: Every effective value has a known source and every partial write preserves unrelated keys

rejection.scenario: A required value that is absent or a read outside authorization fails before use

recovery.scenario: A rejected write leaves the prior snapshot intact; a deferred item stays visible with its reopening condition

mechanisms.title: Credential precedence and store separation
mechanisms.problem: One environment file can serve both as a user-managed environment layer and a Harness-managed secret store, while two credential kinds can resolve in opposite orders. A user then cannot predict which key a request uses, and the UI may disable saving a key merely because the launching shell exports the name.
triggers: A credential can come from a file, process environment, project .env, or user .env
A provider resolver reads its own stored record or a stored reference
A UI edits a credential whose name is also exported
obligations: Keep one file one job: the managed store holds strict CredentialRef to non-empty secret entries; the user environment layer remains separate
Use one deterministic precedence for every provider: managed store, inherited process environment, invocation cwd .env, harness-home .env
A save writes the winning layer; describe reports writable and the supplying source; set/unset never refuse an exported name
Feed provider resolvers from the credential seam before the launch environment
For a one-run override use a separate harness home or remove the stored reference; do not add a per-run flag above the store
Disclose the order in UI help text rather than comparing layers on every resolution

Reject every structural deviation of the credentials document (non-mapping root, non-POSIX key, non-string or empty value, duplicate key, malformed YAML) loudly at boot and write, and on live reload warn while retaining the last good snapshot.

Model discovery is a secret-bearing payload: require full Host API authentication, never store or echo the key, let a typed key win over a stored credential without reconstructing the stored value, and keep credentials out of refusal details while bounding the response by bytes actually received.
steps: Enumerate credential sources and existing precedence rules
Define one ladder and source labels
Route every provider through the credential seam
Make the winning layer writable and report provenance
Migrate/upgrade users whose exported values are now shadowed

enforcement.mode: Ordering tests across providers, write/describe tests, and an upgrade path
enforcement.implementation: The managed store outranks environment; the provider never writes the environment; the UI reports the order
enforcement.trust: A write to the winning layer succeeds even when the name is exported; unreadable layers fall back deterministically
enforcement.failure: Removing the stored reference or using a separate home restores an exported value
enforcement.exceptions: A headless profile may intentionally omit the store and partially supersede the per-run policy; exact file names are source-specific

mechanisms.applicability: Provider credentials with multiple possible sources and a settings UI.

migration.strategy: Choose one precedence and one writable layer, then route all providers through the same seam
migration.implementation: Implement the ladder, provenance reporting, UI copy, and upgrade guide
migration.requiredSupport: A credential seam, source-labeled resolution, and tests across provider families

rejection.scenario: A request never silently uses a lower layer when a stored value exists

recovery.scenario: A user can recover an exported value by removing the stored reference or isolating the harness home

mechanisms.title: Privilege separation and dispatch-time consent
mechanisms.problem: A host-level privilege is not the same as the user's choice of target. Model authority can be widened to support manual work; an object API can be coupled to an interpreter's persistence and cancellation choices; retained native handles can outlive consent; and pointer cleanup or cross-call reservation can silently undo a user interaction.
triggers: A user-operated capability shares a sandbox or process with model-driven work
A native/UI object API is introduced or exposed to model tools
Consent for a target application can be revoked while handles remain alive
obligations: Separate user-operated privileges from model authority; do not widen the Agent sandbox to support manual terminal work
Make the object API independent of the evaluator and platform so input does not inherit unrelated persistence/cancellation choices
Bind consent to a verifiable target identity: canonical executable path plus a verified signing requirement; labels never establish identity
Unverifiable or ad-hoc applications receive task-only access tied to a process instance and connection lifetime; they cannot create saved grants
Prepare metadata and handles before asking, then check the executable again before launch; serialize same-target decisions; avoid re-prompting within a task after refusal
Removing a grant invalidates handles and cancels active operations; reauthorization uses a fresh connection; disposal awaits native cleanup
Keep operations complete and unpressed where required (hover must not press or restore a pointer); do not infer cross-call application ownership from arrival order or Session lifetime
Enforce policy at dispatch, not through model instructions or hidden controls

State the grant exact reach: the user terminal runs as the subprocess provider system user and may write outside the workspace, but grants neither root nor container escape; Session ownership groups and cleans up and never implies Agent authority.

Pin direct user-shell launch across all Agent sandbox modes and retained ownership across mode transitions, with a real PTY scenario for inside and outside writes while Agent denial and approval still hold.
Treat input success as dispatch, not task completion: callers verify effects and never retry uncertain input automatically, and observation must not lock the desktop.
Keep source-generation executables content-addressed so a live executable is never replaced, and separate the package payload published for distribution from the source-build path.

Scope application revocation to the Agent connection: revoking one application also invalidates other application handles on that connection (they need fresh selection), while saved grants remain reusable, task grants expire, and independent connections remain unaffected unless they share the application.

For clipboard paste, bound waiting for the consumer to request the data, close the provider on timeout, restore the clipboard only while ownership holds, and report only that no read occurred within the interval rather than claiming the application never processed the command.
steps: Identify the authority being exercised and its owner
Bind approvals to a verifiable target identity
Ask before side effects and enforce again at dispatch
Revoke by invalidating handles and connections
Test concurrent decisions and revocation

enforcement.mode: Dispatch-time consent checks, OS permissions, and connection invalidation
enforcement.implementation: The executor enforces the decision; the OS authorizes the host; model instructions are never the boundary
enforcement.trust: A missing/revoked grant fails the operation; stale snapshots cannot become valid again
enforcement.failure: A refused operation leaves no side effect; revocation forces fresh selection
enforcement.exceptions: Platform signing, ACL, and native-object semantics are source-specific; packaged permissions and binary distribution may be out of scope

mechanisms.applicability: Native automation, user terminals sharing a machine, and any capability where host privilege exceeds user intent.

migration.strategy: Separate authority, target identity, and consent lifetime before building the API
migration.implementation: Implement identity verification, dispatch checks, revocation, and fresh-connection reauthorization
migration.requiredSupport: A verifiable signing identity, a question/approval service, and native handle cleanup

mechanisms.title: 受管执行范围：进程树只是观察，不是保证
mechanisms.problem: 进程组、Windows 父进程遍历和 PTY 后代扫描只能描述可观察关系；子进程可以 setsid、被重新挂接或在父进程退出后存活，因此终止“看起来的进程树”可能返回，而工作、端口或文件仍被占用。发布 PID 也不能解决问题，因为原生目标身份是异步建立的，PID 不命名受管范围。
triggers: 工具启动子进程、终端或脚本执行
需要取消或超时后确认没有后代存活
工作流/自动化在宿主之外执行模型生成的代码
文件系统与子进程能力同时挂载并为上层提供执行环境
obligations: 在真正执行前由 provider 选出一个私有受管范围所有者；执行后不得只发布 PID 作为终止依据
优先使用平台原生范围：符合条件的 Linux 普通/PTY 进程用 transient user-systemd scope；符合条件的 Windows 普通进程用私有 runner 拥有的、未命名 kill-on-close Job；不支持的主机明确降级到较弱的回退并说明
终止/等待接口控制并观察同一受管范围，`.done` 报告直接目标；不能把“直接目标已退出”当成后代已停止
文件系统与子进程共同定义一个执行世界：路径命名空间、可执行文件、进程与终端会话必须一致；上层能力消费这两个接口，不直接命名某个 provider
复用已有的受限 Node 执行运行时（文件策略、隔离程序状态、受限输出/控制流量、受管清理），不新起第二个执行器
持久执行模式只描述状态保留，不描述进程实现：默认每次调用新进程；显式选择 persistent-in-memory 才按对象身份状态所有者保留 REPL；durable 不是可接受值，除非先定义恢复点、可恢复值和外部资源处理
Never replay a launch after an ambiguous failure: the failure may occur after execution, so replay could execute the command twice; report the failure instead.

Cache only a successful deep containment probe and recheck manager reachability before each eligible call; infer startup failure only from an owner-issued termination signal, not from an unconsumed request, because abort, timeout or disposal can end the launcher first.

Treat fallback containment as observational: sweep descendants before and after terminating the top-level shell, wait on PID-identity-fenced descendants, and state enumerability limits (for example a macOS child reparented between snapshots) instead of claiming a strong guarantee; remote providers must preserve the same consumer contracts or reject unsupported operations rather than duplicating Bash/PTY/LSP.

Preserve caller-controlled lifetime for long workflows with an explicit null rather than a huge numeric deadline; cancellation does not wait for cooperative script progress and disposal waits for child cleanup, so a provider that breaks its lifecycle contract delays disposal, and the managed-range limits still cap what can be claimed.

Never infer quiescence from an unknown or malformed manager result: an unreported process count stays unresolved, malformed combinations reject waitForExit(), and a leftover active unit with no processes is stopped only after the documented proof conditions.

Bind terminal cancellation to the send reservation: retain it while an in-flight write settles, then signal the foreground group; a stale inspection must not release it, a rejected write sends no signal, the absolute deadline stays armed, and close rejects new public signals while delegating quiescence to the handled awaited termination.

Treat the per-spawn selector as a locator, not a credential or persistent format; keep wire records closed (missing, extra, mistyped or unknown fields fail closed), preserve the parent first cancellation reason exactly, and never transmit the cancellation reason.

mechanisms.title: Transport and storage trust derived from receiver state
mechanisms.problem: Advertising an HTTPS URL does not encrypt the listener or establish certificate trust; forwarded headers and public URLs cannot establish proxy identity; and browser storage partitions can either lose preferences or leak credentials across accounts and process restarts.
triggers: A directly reached server must carry credentials
A deployment sits behind a proxy
A desktop shell stores account-scoped browser state
obligations: Let the listener itself own TLS: load certificate and unencrypted private key before binding; invalid or mismatched material fails activation with no HTTP fallback
Derive the bind URL, plain-HTTP warning, and Secure cookie attribute from the listener protocol; never from publicUrl or forwarded headers
Compare Origin by its own HTTP(S) scheme while keeping the listener's scheme for grants; do not equate a proxy's upstream transport with the browser page's scheme
Bind cookie names and signed audiences to the scheme so an HTTP credential cannot replay on HTTPS; keep existing HTTP cookie spelling valid
Leave certificate issuance, trust, renewal, and replacement to the operator; read files once per activation
Partition browser storage by a hash of origin plus a stable account ID, never raw IDs or tokens
A persistent partition keeps only the declared data class (for example localStorage) and clears cookies, filesystem, IndexedDB, caches, service workers, and auth state before loading
Clean up on close and on next open, await cleanup during shutdown, and block the account from reopening until cleanup succeeds
steps: Classify what the receiver actually controls

Derive cookie and storage scoping from receiver state
Clean up on every lifecycle edge and test abnormal exit

enforcement.implementation: The socket and account identity are the trust roots; advertisements and request headers are not

enforcement.failure: A failed cleanup leaves the account blocked until a later cleanup succeeds; other accounts are unaffected
enforcement.exceptions: Certificate lifecycle and production deployment guides remain operator-owned; real browser-process evidence may be separate

mechanisms.applicability: Directly reached servers with credentials and desktop shells that retain account-scoped state.

mechanisms.title: Deadline primitive and per-tool timeout policy
mechanisms.problem: Timeout logic gets reimplemented in several places, fused incorrectly with upstream cancellation, and scattered across tool implementations. Termination is capability-specific, so a shared timer cannot safely kill arbitrary work.
triggers: An asynchronous tool or provider call can hang
A tool needs a different timeout from the default
A timeout must be distinguished from caller cancellation
obligations: Provide one shared deadline/timeoutOf library that owns deadline math, timeout classification, and reason recovery
Attach timeout policy only to model-facing tool execution through an around-dispatch waterfall between pre- and post-dispatch hooks
Require explicit per-tool opt-in; do not impose one global timeout on every tool
Let the capability owner perform termination; the policy layer does not claim it can stop arbitrary work
Distinguish timeout from upstream cancellation and preserve the distinct reason/error

For stream/idle budgets, arm the timer only while one iterator next() is outstanding, disarm on resolution, rearm on later demand, and optionally pulse that same outstanding demand for out-of-band activity; a pulse outside outstanding demand or after disposal is a no-op, concurrent demand fails, disposal clears the active arm, and a sliding idle interval is never a total-call deadline or a charge on consumer think time.

Classify the first abort reason after abort (timeout versus caller cancellation) instead of the thrown error shape; racing causes report one cause, capability-specific timeout codes remain capability-owned, and timeoutOf is scoped to the inner capability so an outer deadline is classified as upstream cancellation.
Do not add a timeout to work that cannot be forced to stop (for example local file syscalls), and delete always-zero or always-false timeout fields that no caller reads.

Declaring timeoutMs is a contract that the tool honors exec.signal and reaches quiescence; never race the tool promise to fake enforcement, and keep timeout out of model-facing schemas while a deployment or provider backstop sits above the tool-call budget.

Compose around-dispatch wrappers by registration order: a wrapper that calls next wraps downstream listeners, one that returns without next short-circuits them, and the deployment chooses whether the budget covers a whole retry or each attempt.

Declare the tool's opt-in and policy

mechanisms.title: Target-neutral presentation assembly and replacement points
mechanisms.problem: A centralized transcript fold or renderer-owned parsing makes every new business node edit switches, replay, indexes, and caches. Running values sit outside the finalized flow and remount; slot priorities encode unrelated semantics; an optional renderer leaves the default outside registration; a shared gallery merges per-domain replacement identity; and per-node projection state grows with the window.
triggers: A UI must project multiple business objects from one event window
Third parties need to replace or wrap one presentation position
A high-frequency stream must display progressively without implying execution
A projection checkpoint grows with message count
obligations: Let Session own only the contiguous event window and snapshot notification; register Event Definitions and per-target View Builders
match(event) reads only the current event and returns a stable id and start/update role; it must not read Contexts or history

Keep one lifecycle per kind+id rather than one start: the earliest start initializes and later starts for the same id update that lifecycle, so independent calls must use distinct ids and a second-start error cannot detect identity reuse; State folds forward from the start and any non-tail insertion or dependency change replays from that start rather than patching backwards
Make Location a first-class engine fact; publish Step data before Turn data; give renderers only stable read-only location data
Separate State updates from publication cadence (immediate, animation frame, none); never let cadence change the fold

Separate a replacement position (Slot) from a reusable implementation (Factory); the official default is an ordinary peer registration; per-domain slots share one implementation without merging replacement identity
Expose progressive tool phases and lazily computed argument views without implying execution; keep history convergent to final state
Retain only non-derivable projection state; bump the state version when the shape changes
Accept the assembled surface at assembly level rather than declaring a taxonomy by hand

Drive incremental argument display from observed source changes and keep unread calls on their prior block reference; schema order and description hints are best effort, so render fields as they arrive and fall back to the title when the tool name arrives after its arguments.

Retire a replaced slot surface rather than aliasing it: update fixtures and the client inspect catalog, keep the replacement position exclusive, and do not auto-compose multiple text transformations; a display transformation is not redaction or model-input modification.

Treat every delta carrying an id as a start candidate: the earliest opens the lifecycle whether or not it is named, later deltas fold as updates, observed-answer changes replace the published root, and a view opened after the name cannot scan arguments that arrived earlier.

Share request-prompt interpretation as a pure function across targets without sharing target state; the first header in a step follows the provider envelope while later headers stay at their own event, non-initial headers outside a loaded window render conservatively, every header is a full snapshot, and prepending a predecessor may hide an unchanged change header without withdrawing its stable Node key.

Keep inbox classification target-owned: register an inbox definition only where a target consumes classification, store only message IDs in immutable splice nodes, materialize the pending chain once per successful claim while replacing the previous claimed set, and retain linear ID state in historical contexts.

mechanisms.title: Live retention distinct from recovery
mechanisms.problem: Restoring a saved URL or caching an element does not preserve a live browsing context. Unmounting a body or changing DOM ancestors disconnects a guest; overlay or reparenting alternatives lose sizing and event semantics. Retention also holds scopes and memory, so it must not be implicit.

A Session switch must not destroy a live embedded page

Opt a type into lazy retention explicitly (keepMounted); create the body on first display and keep it until its occurrence or provider lifetime ends; do not persist the retention policy
Own one SessionReference per view; let tabs contribute retention holds rather than independent references; keep the Session provider key stable
Bind navigation and occupancy only for the selected Session; background actions address their own store; hide content from pointer/keyboard and blur focus
Give the provider physical attach/detach callbacks (hiding emits neither); disposal waits for pending creation/release; an acquisition completing after cancellation is released, not attached
State the retention-versus-recovery table and the cost: no implicit LRU or idle timeout; reclamation needs an explicit suspension/recovery policy

mechanisms.title: Decision-grade performance governance
mechanisms.problem: Storage optimization can move disproportionate work into writes, reads, or forks; font reuse does not reduce image work; and a single performance number can hide a regression in another path.
triggers: A hot path or storage layout changes
A resource budget is proposed
A performance claim is used to justify a design
obligations: Measure representative candidates independently under an explicit methodology: the persistence Note rotates five rebuilds over one corpus, performs three complete/suffix sweeps per build, discards the highest/lowest per metric and averages the remaining three; do not relabel that trimmed mean as a median

Use separate budgets for costs that do not substitute for one another, and name only the cost classes the sources actually measure: stored size versus full-write, read and fork time; font-reuse work versus image decoding/resampling; and a reduced preview image resolution is not an engine memory cap, because the engine can still decode full-resolution sources, load large font collections, or exhaust its build-time memory maximum
State non-guarantees: local measurements are not whole-page or CI latency
Build immutable metadata snapshots once and clone per worker; keep per-worker caches scoped
Verify preview DPI through actual exported image dimensions with selectable text and page count; ABI option forwarding alone cannot establish filter behavior
steps: Define the corpus and the decision the measurement must support
Use the stated rotated five-build persistence method and trimmed mean, keeping exclusions and tradeoffs visible
Set budgets with headroom and non-guarantees
Check complete font keys, snapshot reuse/reload and actual engine export dimensions, not merely ABI forwarding
Re-run on the target platform

enforcement.mode: Documented comparative benchmark methodology plus source font/provider/real-engine behavior tests; no source-declared CI performance threshold
enforcement.implementation: The performance owner records comparable candidates and tradeoffs; preview tests inspect complete keys, snapshot lifetime/reload and real exported image dimensions
enforcement.trust: The evidence supports the measured workload and tested export behavior, not an automatic CI regression budget or a committed persistence benchmark harness absent from the declared sources
enforcement.failure: A failed optimization reverts to the measured baseline rather than shipping an unmeasured claim
enforcement.exceptions: Historical numbers are not current guarantees; no benchmark was executed in this extraction

mechanisms.title: Release identity, validation placement, and ordered publication
mechanisms.problem: Independent versioning of a shell, backend, client, and plugins creates unqualified combinations; a health verdict can claim more than it proves; checks placed after publication cannot protect the release; and a pre-release rename with compatibility aliases leaves two durable vocabularies.
triggers: A packaged application or multi-artifact release is built
A health/readiness verdict gates downstream composition
A feature is renamed before release
Release artifacts are uploaded and channel metadata is published
obligations: Bind one release identity to the exact artifact and its core dependencies; the release cannot select another core version at build or runtime
Reserve the product profile name and reject cross-product package operations
Sign and verify production artifacts; fail rather than produce an unsigned artifact; keep local unsigned mode clearly separate and unable to pass release validation
Validate completion record, versions, channel metadata, artifact names, sizes, and digests before reading credentials or uploading
Upload immutable versioned payloads and all blockmaps first; replace channel metadata last; never delete historical objects needed for differential updates
Make a health verdict prove exactly what consumers infer (for example, broken means will not compose), and place each check where it can prove its claim
For a pre-release rename, update every reference together with no compatibility aliases; keep durable vocabulary stable when compatibility matters

After a pre-release rename the old config values and preset ids are unsupported; do not bump the format version for a rename that leaves durable values unchanged, and give a later durable rename its own adjacent migration edge plus fixture refresh.

Prefer under-reporting to a false broken health verdict: a package that is present but would fail to import may remain healthy and fail at mount, because a false broken makes a usable preset unselectable; keep the verdict independent of any one package build state.

Separate local unsigned packaging from production: strip certificate inputs, isolate artifacts, omit updater configuration and the completion record, and force signed mode for the regular package command rather than letting an environment request downgrade a release.

Replace installed directories by extracting beside the destination, renaming complete directories on the same volume, retaining the old directory through staging, and restoring it if promotion fails; packaged applications ignore development resource and project environment overrides.

Verify every native runtime file and every produced signature before inventory or publication; require notarization and Gatekeeper acceptance for the application and disk image; do not expose channel metadata until the completed signed build and every referenced artifact pass validation.

When products share durable data, each shared owner enforces its format version and process lock before reading, migrating or writing; products must not resolve or install packages from each other node_modules or profile.

Keep signing credentials out of tracked files and system settings: restrict file access, remove temporary CI configuration, exclude real settings from Git and release mappings, sign serially, and stop on the first failure.

Release configuration files are the exclusive source of release fields: stale shell or system credentials must not override them, loading must not mutate the parent environment, and validation must happen before builds, downloads or release-record cleanup.

Scrub every packaging and upload credential from build subprocess environments and write the release completion record only after electron-builder and every signing or notarization hook succeeds; resolve only the public updater URL and disable builder publishing.

Name channels by release maturity: stable releases use `latest`, a prerelease uses the first semver prerelease identifier, and a release id embedded in the update URL is immutable so an upload must reject a different id; a random directory reduces guessability but is not authentication.
steps: Define release identity and artifact ownership
Validate mode-specific inputs before any build or upload
Sign, verify, and (where required) notarize
Upload artifacts first, then channel metadata; publish only after completion
Test previous-version installation and update on each blocking platform

enforcement.mode: Release gates, signature/notarization verification, Gatekeeper, digest/version checks, and ordered upload
enforcement.implementation: The release owner binds versions; signing infrastructure verifies identity; the platform verifies trust; repository tests alone cannot qualify a release
enforcement.trust: Any missing signature, mismatched digest, or failed verification stops the release before publication
enforcement.failure: A failed publication leaves historical artifacts and the prior channel metadata intact; local unsigned artifacts cannot pass release validation
enforcement.exceptions: Production signing, hosting, and update infrastructure were not exercised; platform-specific requirements remain external

mechanisms.applicability: Packaged desktop applications and any multi-artifact release with independent shell/backend/plugin versions.

migration.strategy: Bind the release identity and freeze version selection
migration.implementation: Validate inputs, sign, verify, and stage immutable artifacts
migration.requiredSupport: Ordered publication plus a completion record and release-environment tests

positive.scenario: A released artifact set is exactly the validated one and updates from the prior supported version succeed

rejection.scenario: A mismatched version/digest, missing signature, or false health claim stops the release

recovery.scenario: A failed upload leaves prior metadata and historical artifacts usable

mechanisms.limitations: Signing identities, update infrastructure, and platform GUI evidence require production resources; no release command or remote operation was run during extraction.

mechanisms.title: 存储事实的始终开启不可变所有权
mechanisms.problem: “存储后不再变”如果只靠可选 dev 插件或 TypeScript readonly，就既可能在生产中被关掉，也可能在运行时被擦除或强转。没有单一运行时边界时，校验与存储可能因有状态 getter 而给出不同结果，调用方引用也会被保留，日志中的事实仍可被外部修改。
triggers: 一个对象即将进入持久化事件日志
已存储事件被发布给观察者或 eventAt
有人提议用 dev-only 插件或 readonly 类型保证不可变
快照、seed 或派生事件走不同的写入路径
obligations: 在 Session/存储运行时内强制不可变所有权，始终开启；不做成可选 dev 插件
一次递归遍历生成无损 JSON 快照，拒绝不支持的值，并产出真正进入日志的分离记录；校验与存储共用这一份结果
在接受事件及其后代发布前深度冻结；append 返回被拥有的冻结事件，观察者与 eventAt 收到同一记录
snapshotEvents 返回不会增长的冻结数组快照；seq 只读长度而不物化；seed 走同一 validation/snapshot/freeze 边界；deriveMessages 另行产生分离、深冻结的 Message 投影与新数组快照，不是派生事件回写日志
不要用 TypeScript readonly 作为运行时保证：它会被擦除、可被强转，并会污染可变消费者
任何调用方引用、getter 或有状态转换都不得留到发布之后
steps: 列出 append/seed 等进入存储的路径，另列 deriveMessages 的只读投影边界；不要把投影当成 append 事件
在运行时做一个递归 JSON 物化与拒绝步骤
在同一路径上深冻结并发布同一记录
让快照/seq 读取遵守不增长、不物化契约
测试外部修改、getter 差异、不支持值和 seed 路径

enforcement.mode: runtime-enforced always-on boundary
enforcement.implementation: Session 内部递归快照 + 深冻结；append/观察者返回同一冻结记录；dev 插件与 readonly 类型都不是边界
enforcement.trust: 运行时是唯一强制点；类型系统只提供编译期提示
enforcement.failure: 不支持的值或非 JSON 值在进入日志前被拒绝；发布后修改尝试在严格模式下抛错
enforcement.exceptions: 同一始终开启的存储语义也适用于 focused tests 与 custom embedding；冻结单个记录不建立跨记录序列、嵌套、tool pairing 或 request reconstruction 关系，那些由其他规则验证

mechanisms.applicability: 事件溯源日志、持久化不可变记录、以及任何“校验后存储”的事实对象。

migration.strategy: 把不可变所有权收进运行时，再删除 dev 插件与 readonly 假设
migration.implementation: 统一 append/seed 的快照与冻结边界；deriveMessages 单独返回分离、冻结的 Message 投影，缓存只复用安全不可变投影，观察者读取被拥有的存储记录
migration.requiredSupport: 运行时存储边界、递归 JSON 校验、冻结行为测试、对快照/seq 的契约测试

positive.scenario: append 返回的对象已冻结，观察者收到同一记录，快照不会随后增长

rejection.scenario: 外部修改、getter 导致校验/存储不一致、或未走统一路径的 seed 被识别为缺陷

recovery.scenario: 不支持的值在写入前失败且不产生半条记录；focused/custom composition 也保持相同存储语义；request-side 变更不能通过 deriveMessages 到达存储历史

mechanisms.title: Session context ownership and explicit defaults
mechanisms.problem: Provider readers read ambient agent context or a module-level CWD and the consumer may be undefined. Implicitly deriving CWD from a raw process value lets one Session observe another's choice; optional provider defaults can mask a missing Context selection; optional overrides let unrelated parts of one view derive different identities.
triggers: A provider receives an optional context or a process-global working directory
A tool resolves paths against a module-level process.cwd()
A renderer composes several optional overrides
obligations: Require the provider's own context explicitly; do not fall back to a request-scoped agent context
The provider must never read the agent's Session selection; the consumer carries the choice
Only the provider's configuration defines a default/current CWD; a missing value is the explicit default, not a guess
Use a workspace identity that follows symlinks and parent traversal consistently; never display a raw process.cwd() as Session cwd
Treat the Context as the fallback after explicit inputs
Resolve a composition once and pass the result to every consumer so one view has one identity
Persist only the whole normalized root; re-derive dependent state before reuse
Omit optional overrides instead of using a sentinel or a second independent default per consumer

Use a process-local initiating identity only for cross-cutting infrastructure; treat ambient presence as neither liveness nor authorization, keep cancellation and ownership explicit, and never let it cross worker, process, HTTP or durable-queue boundaries.

Reach quiescence before disabling the ambient store: dispose HMR and the root first, call the ambient store disable only then, and guard service state so a later boundary cannot re-enter the disposed instance.

Validate the working directory at use and log recovery because it can disappear outside the harness; if neither the current directory nor its recovery destination exists, reject prompt assembly instead of inventing a fallback.

Keep the directory identity visible as required runtime context even when optional context is suppressed, and migrate every consumer (filesystem, shell, instructions, skills, subagents, both SDKs) together.

Keep the inherited Session seed before the child initial task and return guidance, add no child-only request-head material or differing tool schema when parent and child share a preset, and test assembled request-head equality rather than claiming provider cache reuse.

Teardown order for ambient identity: reject new boundaries, drain injected dependents and active returned-Promise boundaries, then disable the store; release nested boundary chains started by an owning fiber unload so teardown never waits on itself, and make post-disposal initiator access throw.
steps: Make the context provider-required and consumer-passed
Remove ambient reads and module-global CWDs
Define the explicit default and one normalization rule
Resolve a composition once; pass it down
Test switching Sessions and path identity

enforcement.mode: Typechecked required parameters plus context tests; path normalization tests
enforcement.implementation: The provider owns the default; the Session owns its cwd; the tool uses the passed value; no consumer may re-default
enforcement.trust: A missing required context fails type/runtime checks; one composition cannot derive two identities
enforcement.failure: Switching back restores the same normalized identity; a deleted workspace fails explicitly
enforcement.exceptions: Repository layout and the context framework are source-specific; no Session-switching execution was performed

mechanisms.applicability: Providers and tools reachable from multiple Sessions or concurrent consumers.

migration.strategy: Separate the provider's own state from the agent's request context
migration.implementation: Require explicit context and define one default
migration.requiredSupport: Context injection, path normalization, and composition resolution

positive.scenario: Two Sessions never share an implicit cwd, and one composed view has one identity

rejection.scenario: A missing context or conflicting per-consumer default is rejected

recovery.scenario: A removed workspace fails clearly rather than silently falling back

mechanisms.title: Single launcher and explicit profile mounting
mechanisms.problem: A private Node application fan out into SDK runtime, desktop host, and CLI duplicated bootstrapping, composition, and environment setup. A minimal profile then mounts all base services, imports most of the graph, and serves trusted pages anyway. Mounting a feature by default makes every profile pay for it.
triggers: Several executables or hosts boot the same application
A minimal/basic configuration is introduced
A packaged runtime must match development behavior
A caller must choose a plugin set
obligations: Route every host through one launcher that owns environment/config loading, logging, Home and plugin resolution, runtime creation, and shutdown
Define base services once; a profile adds or omits only what it declares, with inheritance and product overrides resolved at one point
Never advertise or start a service the profile omits; refuse unknown/banned config keys instead of ignoring them
Mount an explicit roster: only modules the profile lists are loaded; never mount the entire graph by default
Preserve packaged-runtime parity: the launcher must resolve the same built modules and config as development
Omission beats hiding an unusable feature behind config

A standalone minimal profile changes only through its owning bundle or a trusted higher patch that expands it; do not achieve minimality by filtering a full profile, and accept the deliberate duplication of a small complete tree.

Do not reintroduce a Python-owned cordis argument or environment-selected complete config, a second minimal startup plugin, or packaging divergence; profile selection alone separates applications, and both choices keep one launcher, one profile vocabulary and one packaged runtime.
steps: Enumerate every entry point and its bootstrap responsibilities
Move environment/config/plugin resolution into the launcher
Define the profile roster and inheritance rules
Mount only declared modules and validate config keys
Test parity across dev/desktop/CLI and read-only opt-out

enforcement.mode: Launcher boot tests, profile roster/dependency gates, and packaged-runtime smoke tests
enforcement.implementation: The launcher owns startup; the profile declares the roster; the runtime mounts only that roster
enforcement.trust: An omitted service is absent rather than a runtime stub; unknown config fails
enforcement.failure: A failed startup leaves no partially mounted service claimed as ready
enforcement.exceptions: The product launcher, profiles, and packaging were not inspected; no packaged boot was executed

mechanisms.applicability: Applications with multiple hosts (SDK, desktop, CLI) and configurable plugin rosters.

migration.strategy: Enumerate hosts and bootstrap responsibilities
migration.implementation: Build one launcher and explicit profile mounting
migration.requiredSupport: A launcher API, profile definitions, and parity tests

positive.scenario: All hosts start the same way and a minimal profile loads only its roster

rejection.scenario: An undeclared module or unknown key is rejected at startup

recovery.scenario: A failed boot does not leave hidden functionality active

mechanisms.title: Registry resolution and dependency-confusion safety
mechanisms.problem: The default npm registry can be unreachable while a private fallback is configured to host application dependencies. If a package name exists in both, install can resolve from the wrong registry. Combinations can also fail for reasons unrelated to the registry.
triggers: A dependency install/upgrade targets a registry
The default registry is unreachable
A private registry is configured as a fallback or the only source
An installation attempt fails
obligations: Before installing, resolve a registry plan and read the package manager's live registry configuration; never assume the default means public npm
A private registry must never fall through to a public registry for names it is meant to own
Attribute a failure to the registry only when that registry could actually change the outcome (missing package or authentication there); connection or upstream errors are not registry verdicts
Use a bounded liveness check with an explicit timeout and no unbounded hang
Start installation at a registry that is alive now; do not cache a stale reachability verdict across a later attempt
Restore files changed by a failed attempt before retrying
Show which registry each package resolved from and persist the user's registry choice
Remember the chosen registry per window/browser; do not silently switch
steps: Resolve the plan and read the live registry config
Check each registry's reachability within a bound
Install from a live registry and restore files between attempts
Attribute failures correctly and report the resolved source
Remember the choice and test the fallback path

enforcement.mode: Registry-plan tests, failure-attribution tests, bounded timeout, and fail-closed dependency ownership
enforcement.implementation: The package manager is the source of registry truth; the plugin manager attributes failures; no automatic public fallback
enforcement.trust: An unreachable or ambiguous registry fails rather than silently switching to a public one
enforcement.failure: A failed attempt is restored before retry; a remembered choice survives within its stated scope
enforcement.exceptions: No network, registry, or install was exercised; the note's product commands and package names are source-specific

mechanisms.applicability: Plugin/package installation where a private fallback registry coexists with a public default.

migration.strategy: Read the actual registry configuration and map name ownership
migration.implementation: Fail closed on ambiguous/private names, bound liveness, and restore before retry
migration.requiredSupport: Live registry inspection, failure classification, and a registry-choice store

positive.scenario: Each package resolves from its intended registry and a failure is attributed to a registry that could change it

rejection.scenario: An ambiguous private/public name or an unreachable registry stops rather than falls through

recovery.scenario: Files from a failed attempt are restored; a retry uses current liveness

mechanisms.title: Immutable generations and cache publication boundaries
mechanisms.problem: Resolving plugins only at startup forces a restart for any change. A naive reload mutates a partial graph, mixes config and module caches, and leaves old modules and dependents live. Invalidation also has to distinguish real publication points from intermediate disk or build state.
triggers: A runtime must pick up plugin/config changes without a full restart
A cache or resolver memoizes a module/config result
A build or deploy completes but dependents are not yet refreshed
A hot update must ask whether existing identity is retained
obligations: Compute a complete immutable generation, validate it, then publish it into the active resolvers in one reference swap
Never mutate the active graph in place; stop old generation rows only after the successor is valid
Build every successor completely before publishing; a failed validation leaves the current generation active
Key resolved modules, configs, and dependents by generation so an old cache cannot answer for a new generation
Retained identity requires a purposeful restart or service shutdown, not an implicit cache-miss
Model disk/build success and live publication as separate points; invalidate dependents at the real publication point, not merely on write
When swapping configuration and module graphs, invalidate separately; one invalidation does not imply the other
Key invalidation on real anchors such as source paths, module identity, and config files; prefer conservative missing of an invalidation over stale reuse
Replace or invalidate caches owned by the old generation; do not let a stale resolved target keep serving
Inherit the generation boundary into Workers and revalidate retained references against the published link target

Own the package-name interception surface: resolution entries occupy package names in the profile node_modules, preserve native ancestor order and per-position peer mappings, and keep installation-scope directories outside linked interception.

Treat generation construction as startup or update work, not resolve work; the resolve hot path stays scope classification, bare-name extraction, local-before-fallback selection, a map lookup, and one native resolution.

Accept one package identity per process: a resolution-table swap cannot invalidate live module instances or object references, so retained identities require restart, and removing profile records or linked roots must not be mistaken for unloading modules.
Bootstrap each owned Worker early and self-contain its loader; provide no disk-only backend or dual comparison mode.

Validate successor compatibility on a retained-identity allow/deny matrix: profile-scope mappings and local names may be removed, but a retained installation entry directory, version and declaring anchor must not change; moving a mapping requires removal plus reinstall.
Keep every loaded namespace for entries sharing a name and base URL; an uninitialized entry must not erase another entry imported namespace, and the loaded URL remains the reload unit.

Expire configuration-only manifests with module caches rather than reloading modules; keep JSON modules on ordinary dependency reloads, and when HMR is disabled or a startup disablement is pending, defer further publication until restart while preserving running plugin mappings.
Re-test the resolver and HMR compatibility suite on every Node upgrade because the implementation depends on internal interfaces.

Keep the routing surface narrow and deterministic: ignore builtins, relative and absolute paths, URLs, parents outside the profiles and registered roots, and CommonJS requests with explicit paths; keep self-references on the original parent and let native probes decide legacy subpath continuation.

Recompose in order: stop rows the generation no longer lists while their packages are still mapped, then publish the latest generation exactly once; a resolution constructed as plain data cannot be refreshed.
steps: Define the generation and its validation rule
Build a complete successor without touching active state
Publish with a single swap and stop old rows
Invalidate generation-scoped caches at the publication point
Test abandoned builds, mixed config/module updates, Worker inheritance, and retained links

enforcement.mode: Generation validation and swap tests, Node internal compatibility matrix, HMR generation tests, and retained-reference validation
enforcement.implementation: The runtime owns the active generation; resolvers return generation-scoped values; caches cannot serve across generations
enforcement.trust: An invalid successor is abandoned with the old generation still active; a stale generation-scoped cache hit is treated as a bug
enforcement.failure: A failed swap keeps the prior generation serving; a retained reference either validates against the new target or is restarted
enforcement.exceptions: Depends on Node/source internals; no built Worker or real HMR run was performed

mechanisms.applicability: Runtime plugin display internals, dev-server HMR, and build/publication pipelines.

migration.strategy: Define a generation and its validation boundary
migration.implementation: Build and swap instead of mutating in place
migration.requiredSupport: Generation-aware resolvers, one publication point, and cache ownership

positive.scenario: A change becomes visible through exactly one published generation

rejection.scenario: A partial successor, mixed cache, or invalid retained link is rejected

recovery.scenario: A failed build/swap leaves the previous generation fully serving

mechanisms.title: Staged migration without permanent compatibility debt
mechanisms.problem: Large refactors run for several iterations with old and new APIs coexisting. Contributors need to know which API is target, which is legacy, and what each stage may change. A compatibility path without a real consumer or removal condition becomes permanent, and stage status drifts.
triggers: A multi-stage refactor is in flight across many contributors
Old and new APIs coexist
Stage-specific rules apply to different call sites
obligations: Publish one operating protocol for each application type plus one private provider protocol; state the single stage change each stage may make
Each stage is behavior-preserving or performs exactly one named change; no stage bundles unrelated changes
A compatibility path exists only with a real consumer and a removal condition; name both
Write a stage table (stage, target state, allowed change, forbidden change) and keep it current
Use a switchable warn-then-enforce gate: warn while existing violations are fixed, enforce for new code, then remove the warn mode
State invariants that hold in every stage
Make the FAQ route each question to its normative owner instead of duplicating rules
Give contributors a reading order: overview, protocols, current-stage entry, then stage table
Land each stage as an independently revertible commit boundary with one ownership result, named compatibility limits, and focused characterization tests.
Update the owning note, subsystem reference, package documentation, generated catalogs, and required bilingual pair in the same change as the stage.

Name non-goals explicitly (for example format, wire values, SDK output, or model-visible history) so migration cannot smuggle behavior changes; contract tests cover freshness, close durability, migration preparation, and cross-process ownership.

Handoff records current state, target, gap, next removal condition, and exact branch and commit; migrate one caller-backed path at a time and keep lifecycle, format, and failure-order changes in separate stages.
A dependency gate checks that ordinary plugins do not import concrete providers; compatibility entries carry coverage, a named old consumer, and a removal condition, with no migration allowlist.

A thin abstraction must not hide lifecycle gaps: alternate implementations cannot participate until the service owns publication and attachment, and a synchronous disposer must not start an unowned asynchronous close.
Review the FAQ whenever a stage updates overview status, and keep current branch types, tests and subsystem documentation authoritative over FAQ answers.

Pick one caller and migrate it through the contract
Add contract tests and run the warn gate
Enforce for new code and remove warnings
Record current state, target state, and gap per stage

enforcement.implementation: The protocol is the single standard; CI enforces the active gate; reviewers route disputes to the named owner
enforcement.trust: An unreferenced compatibility alias or stage-forbidden change fails review; a gate cannot be bypassed by new code
enforcement.failure: A failed stage keeps the previous stage's contracts; a rolled-back change removes its compatibility path
enforcement.exceptions: Most Notes are proposals or plans rather than implemented stages; stage status can drift from code

mechanisms.applicability: Large in-flight refactors with multiple contributors and coexisting APIs.

rejection.scenario: A permanent alias, unrelated bundled change, or stage-forbidden edit is rejected

recovery.scenario: A failed/rolled-back stage restores the prior contract and drops the new path

mechanisms.title: Required cancellation signals across async capability seams
mechanisms.problem: Optional signals let callers omit cancellation, so cancellation silently fails to propagate. Deriving work without linking it to the parent signal leaves work running after the caller is gone. A required signal can also be faked with a never-aborting default.

Work is started on behalf of a caller that may cancel
A handoff transfers ownership of the operation
obligations: Require an AbortSignal on in-scope async capability calls; make it a required parameter, not an option
Inventory the real scope from the tool execution contract and reachable async work; do not declare the whole repository in scope
Link every derived signal to its parent so abort propagates transitively
Never supply a never-aborting default or read an ambient async-local signal
Do not revalidate cancellation in runtime dispatch if the seam already requires it; avoid duplicated mechanisms
Exclude synchronous work and work that has already been handed off; name the handoff commit point
A handoff must transfer cancellation ownership explicitly at one commit point
steps: Inventory in-scope calls from the tool execution contract
Change the seam to require a signal
Link derived signals
Add compile-fail tests for omitted signals
Verify integration quiescence on abort

enforcement.implementation: The type system enforces presence; the seam owner propagates; runtime does not silently supply a default
enforcement.trust: An omitted signal fails compilation; an aborted caller leaves no child work
enforcement.failure: A handoff that has committed continues under its new owner; cancellation after handoff is not claimed
enforcement.exceptions: The Notes are a proposal; some findings are source-traced only. Mechanical compliance (passing a signal) does not prove correct linking

migration.requiredSupport: Compile-enforced signatures and integration cancellation tests

mechanisms.title: Consumer-first disposal for dependent resources
mechanisms.problem: Shutdown or plugin replacement disposes provider resources while consumers still need them for cleanup. A consumer that stops new admission and waits for accepted work can still find its storage already closed, so cleanup fails at exactly the moment it matters.
triggers: A provider is replaced or shut down while consumers remain
